The Over 8.0 sits at +103 best versus a median of even money, generating 73.9 edge_bps and positive expected value at a plus-money price. Griffin Jax is a reliever being used as a starter for Tampa Bay, suggesting a shorter leash and potential for a bullpen game that inflates run totals. The Under 7.0 shows 208.6 edge_bps at -114 versus a median of -124, meaning FanDuel is significantly more generous than the rest of the market on the under side. Emerson Hancock is a legitimate strikeout arm for Seattle and Austin Warren is a low-leverage reliever masquerading as a starter for the Mets, which should limit run production early. A 7.0 total is already low but both pitching situations favor keeping this game under.

The Under 8.0 carries a 179.8 edge_bps at -107 versus a median of -115 across 9 books, representing nearly 2% of implied probability reclaimed. Jacob deGrom on the mound for Texas is a dominant ace when healthy and capable of suppressing any offense; paired against Michael McGreevy for St. Louis, the Rangers' starter gives this game a clear elite-versus-average pitching dynamic. At -107 versus -115 median, this is one of the sharpest total prices on the board today.

Arizona +1.5 shows 193.9 edge_bps at -111 versus a median of -120, a meaningful gap across all 9 books. Eduardo Rodriguez starting for Arizona is a serviceable left-hander against Emmet Sheehan for LA, and the Dodgers -1.5 run line at +106 best indicates oddsmakers see this as a close contest despite the h2h moneyline spread. Getting the D-backs to avoid a 2+ run loss at near-even money is strong value given the competitive pitching matchup.

Miami at +132 shows 174 edge_bps versus a median of +123, with BetOnline and LowVig both sitting 9 points above the market midpoint. Sandy Alcantara, when healthy, is a legitimate ace-level starter for the Marlins and represents a significant pitching upgrade over Washington's Cade Cavalli. At plus money with genuine line value and the superior starter on the mound, this is a worthwhile underdog play.

ig_carousel_topic.topic: Why your win rate matters less than your ROI
ig_carousel_topic.slide1_text: Your win rate is lying to you.
ig_carousel_topic.slide2_text: Most bettors chase 60%+ win rates and think that's the goal. A 60% bettor on -130 favorites is actually losing money long-term. Win rate without odds context is a vanity stat.
ig_carousel_topic.slide3_text: ROI tells you what you actually made per dollar risked. A 54% bettor hitting +110 underdogs can crush a 62% bettor grinding -150 chalk. The number that matters is units, not wins.
ig_carousel_topic.slide4_text: Real example: Bettor A goes 60-40 on -140 favorites. Net: roughly -2.0u. Bettor B goes 54-46 on +105 underdogs. Net: roughly +8.2u. Same sample. Bettor B wins more money.
ig_carousel_topic.slide5_text: SmarterPicks sits at 54.4% on the season with +48.5u and 9.3% ROI across 55 days. Win rate is the headline. ROI is the paycheck.
ig_carousel_topic.caption: Win rate looks good on paper. ROI is what hits your bankroll. 54.4% win rate, +48.5u, 9.3% ROI this season. The math is in the bio.
